title: Design System: Next In Research — The Library Record

flame-bright.displayName: Bright Flame (legacy coral — punctuation on cloth grounds only)

display.purpose: Hero masthead only — extrabold Bricolage Grotesque in paper-bright on the flame field.

headline.purpose: Section and page openers. Headings begin sections directly; no eyebrow labels above them.

title.purpose: Card and slip headings on ephemera objects.

body.purpose: Public Sans narrative prose; leads at 1.125rem; columns capped near 65ch.

label.purpose: Courier Prime bold uppercase document labels printed on ephemera (ledger captions, HOLD FOR:, table headers, chips, pocket labels).

data.purpose: Courier Prime catalog facts — call numbers, dates, agenda rows, captions, statuses, mentor bios. Ledger totals step up to 20px bold.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Resting shadow of catalog cards, slips, table, albums.

shadows.name: print
shadows.purpose: Photo prints and the portrait prints mounted on catalog and coordinator cards.

shadows.name: print-lg
shadows.purpose: The most-lifted objects: hero carousel frame, symposium agenda card, ledger, schedule finale card, students-page feature card; hover state of contact cards.

shadows.name: nav-scrolled
shadows.purpose: Under the fixed nav bar, only after 12px of scroll.

shadows.name: pocket-lip
shadows.purpose: Upward shadow on the card-pocket front panel.

shadows.name: hole-punch
shadows.purpose: Drilled depth inside every rod hole.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.value: spring(stiffness 420, damping 21) from { opacity: 0, scale: 1.45, rotate: rest−5° } to rest; whileInView once, margin −40px
motion.purpose: The site's single authored entrance — things arrive the way a rubber stamp lands. Stamps only.

motion.name: straighten
motion.purpose: Tilted prints/slips and the carousel frame rotate to 0° on hover; pocket cards lift 12px on hover/focus-within.

motion.name: reel-crossfade
motion.purpose: Hero cover carousel. Pauses on hover/focus, stops permanently on any manual control, skips autoplay under prefers-reduced-motion; covers preloaded on mount.

motion.name: hover-color
motion.purpose: Default hover grammar for buttons, links, tabs, chips — color only, never lift or scale.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" around the app + global CSS kill switch (~0ms durations) + matchMedia guard before carousel autoplay
motion.purpose: Three-layer reduced-motion honor: Framer springs, CSS transitions, and autoplay all stand down.

narrative.overview:
The site is a public library's own record of a summer — but the record is now dressed in the program's own brand color. Flame-orange fields (user-pinned, Aug 2026) open and close the record like a poster pasted to the library door; buckram-cloth green remains as the institution's furniture — the nav bar, the footer, the ledger and schools bands; and between them, clean paper neutrals carry the content as physical objects: a card, a slip, a print, a ledger, a pocket. Evidence is the aesthetic. A date is stamped, a mentor is filed under a call number, a photo is a white-bordered archival print with a typed caption. The world explicitly refuses both the dark SaaS gradient hero and the sterile white nonprofit template (direction contract, index.html, seed 1ec49fef, rev. 2), and it retired the warm manila card stock of the first rendition — the paper is clean now, not yellowed.

The mood is civic, warm, and matter-of-fact — a well-run county institution with something to announce, not a startup. Density is generous but orderly: a flame band announces, paper bands present the evidence, cloth bands do the bookkeeping, and objects sit slightly tilted as if just set down. The typography splits cleanly into three voices — poster capitals for announcements, plain civic sans for talking to families, and typewriter mono for anything a librarian would type or stamp.
keyCharacteristics: Two colored registers over one paper ground: flame orange announces (hero, closing field, primary buttons), cloth green administers (nav, footer, ledger, schools band). Never a plain white page.
Clean paper neutrals (#F3F1EC family) as the card stock — the warm manila is retired.
Ephemera as components: catalog cards, hold slips, the accession ledger, card pockets, rod holes, archival prints, and one autoplaying reel of prints (the hero carousel).
Two stamp inks carry all status: red for what happened, blue for what is pending.
Strictly rectilinear paper edges; the only circles are drilled holes and dots.
One authored motion: things arrive the way a rubber stamp lands.
A single light world — no dark mode; the cloth greens are the dark register.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Flame announces, cloth administers. Flame fields open and close the record (hero and closing band) and fill the primary action on paper; cloth is the institution's furniture — nav, footer, ledger band, schools band. Paper bands carry the evidence between them. Neither register ever grounds a whole interior page; those are paper.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Status is always a stamp, and the ink states the tense: red (#BE3A27) for what happened (HELD, a stamped date), blue (#2F5A77) for what's pending (DUE, HOLD FOR, in processing). No green/amber/gray status pills exist in this world.

rules.name: The Card, Not Page Rule
rules.body: Paper-bright surfaces are always bounded objects — bordered in paper-shade, shadowed, often tilted or rod-holed — sitting on a paper, cloth, or flame field. There is no edge-to-edge white or off-white "page."

rules.name: The Typed Data Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime is reserved for what a librarian would type or stamp: identifiers, dates, statuses, captions, labels, and the contents of catalog cards. It never sets narrative prose paragraphs or display headings.

rules.name: The No Floating Label Rule
rules.body: Small mono labels exist only as printed parts of ephemera objects (a slip's header, a ledger's caption, a pocket's label). No eyebrow/kicker labels float above display headings; sections open with the heading itself.

rules.name: The Ink-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are diffuse, downward, and ink-tinted (rgba(32,49,59,…)). Elevation is reserved: card at rest, print for photographs, print-lg only for a band's single hero object. Hover may swap card → print-lg (contact cards) but never invents new shadows.

rules.name: The Guillotine Rule
rules.body: Corners are square because paper is cut, not molded. The only permitted circles are holes and dots. Rounding anything else breaks the material.

rules.name: The Handed-Reel Rule
rules.body: Autoplay is a courtesy, never a takeover: the hero reel pauses while hovered or focused, any manual control (dot, arrow, or the aria-pressed pause toggle) stops autoplay for good, and under prefers-reduced-motion the reel never advances on its own.

dos: Do keep the two registers straight: flame (#B93C15) grounds announcement fields and primary buttons, cloth (#1D4A40/#14352E) grounds the institutional chrome (nav, footer, ledger, schools), and paper (#F3F1EC) grounds content bands. Seam a colored field to paper with an 8px rule in that field's deep tone; seam paper to paper with an ink/10 hairline.

Do render every standalone photograph as a PhotoPrint: white border, shadow-print, slight tilt, hover-straighten, typed mono caption. Portraits mounted inside catalog and coordinator cards keep the white mount but sit square and full-width (4:5 crop).
Do carry status with stamps in the correct ink — red = happened, blue = pending — using the double-ring Stamp and its spring entrance (stiffness 420, damping 21).
Do honor reduced motion at all three layers: MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" around the app, the global CSS kill switch, and a matchMedia guard before any autoplay.
Do give autoplaying media the Handed-Reel treatment: pause on hover/focus, a visible aria-pressed pause control, and permanent stop on any manual navigation.
Do put scroll-mt-16 on any in-page anchor target; the 64px nav is fixed.
Do keep Courier Prime for typed data and labels, Public Sans for prose, Bricolage for headings — three voices, never swapped.
Do give each paper object its full kit: 1px paper-shade border, ink-tinted shadow, square corners, and a rod hole when it's a catalog record.
Do limit icons to functional wayfinding lucide strokes (arrows, chevrons, mail, external-link, menu/x, play/pause) at 16–20px.
donts: Don't round a corner. Only rod holes, dot markers, and the reel dots are circles (The Guillotine Rule).
Don't warm the neutrals back toward manila or cream — the card stock is the clean paper trio (#F3F1EC / #FDFCFA / #E1DED6); the manila rendition is retired by the user.
Don't set flame-bright (#EE6C4D) as text or accents on paper surfaces — it lives as small punctuation on cloth grounds, and the contrast fails anywhere lighter.
Don't float eyebrow/kicker labels above headings; mono labels belong inside ephemera objects only.
Don't introduce a dark mode or new dark surfaces; the cloth greens are this light civic world's entire dark register.
Don't author new entrance animations — the stamp-in spring is the only arrival; everything else is a functional fade, reveal, or straighten at 180–550ms.
Don't use pure-black or colored shadows; every shadow tints from catalog ink rgba(32,49,59,…).
Don't let transformed objects widen the page — tilts and pre-animation scale are why overflow-x: clip is load-bearing on html/body.
